Jacques Moretti and his wife, Jessica, are already under criminal investigation over the deadly blaze at Le Constellation in Crans-Montana.

data.title: French centre-left candidate launches presidential bid amid divided left
data.description: Centre-left politician Raphaël Glucksmann on Sunday launched his bid for the French presidency, aiming to unite moderate left-wing voters and challenge Jean-Luc Mélenchon’s influence ahead of France’s 2027 election. With Marine Le Pen leading first-round polls, Glucksmann is seeking to position himself as a pro-European, pro-Ukraine alternative to both the far right and hard left.

data.title: Thousands rally in Sweden to protest climate policies ahead of general election
data.description: Some 10,000 people rallied in Stockholm on Sunday to demand stronger action on climate change, weeks before Sweden’s general election. data.title: Zelensky rejects wartime elections, saying vote would 'split' Ukraine
data.description: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky has said that holding elections during wartime would pose a threat to the country, following a controversial call by his former defense minister to pave the way for an election. According to the latest opinion poll by the Kyiv Institute of Sociology carried out this summer, only 15 per cent of those surveyed want an election to be held at this time. Details by Eliza Herbert.

data.title: Greek Ithaca island hopes for big tourism boost thanks to Odyssey movie
data.description: Greece's most famous islands have spent this year fighting to keep tourists out... with Santorini and Mykonos now capping cruise arrivals and charging steep entry fees just to manage the crowds. But on one small island, they're hoping for the opposite problem. Ithaca, the legendary home of Homer's Ulysses, is banking on a Hollywood boost, as Christopher Nolan's Odyssey draws new attention to a corner of Greece that's largely stayed off the tourist map. Story by Camille Knight.

data.title: How will European politicians react to a summer of extreme heat?

Answer with Stefan Eye-cot, professor of sociology at the University of Hamburg.

data.title: Venezuela: Two months after the quake, 12,500 people still live in temporary camps
data.description: Two months after two earthquakes struck Venezuela, more than 12,500 people are still living in temporary camps in La Guaira. Many survivors are still struggling to come to terms with the loss of loved ones and their homes. They have been forced to adapt to precarious living conditions, exposed to the elements, with little access to medical care and humanitarian aid. France 24 reporters Herminia Fernández and Julio Uribarris visited three camps housing earthquake survivors.

data.title: What is postpartum psychosis, the illness at the centre of Lindsay Clancy's murder trial?

data.title: When my husband died in a surfing accident, life as I knew it was destroyed. Ten years on, this is what I’ve learned about grief
data.description: One crashing wave on one single day changed everything for our family. How would I keep going? Before they enter the water, surfers will study the ocean. They consider wind and tide conditions. They analyse currents and patterns, break points and swells. They try to read the waves. I have travelled across oceans and a day to sit here on Tamarama beach in Sydney on a high-tide weekday morning in 2024. A notebook and pen lie beside me on the sand as I, too, attempt to read the waves, to find meaning in their unfathomable churn. These past 10 years, this beach has loomed large in my mind. Even when absent, it’s as if my face has been turned to these waves and I have been buffeted, sometimes staggering, sometimes falling, always bracing for the next set to roll in. For I have learned that all it takes is one ocean, one day, to come along and knock you off your feet. Continue reading...

data.title: Pine-cone grenades and planet-baking carbon: the French fires 170 years in the making – a visual guide
data.description: An 1857 decree to drain swamps and plant a monoculture, detritus from the trees and global heating combined to produce the conditions for the Gironde inferno The ruinous fires that overran parts of France this summer have burned more land than ever recorded, forced more people from their homes than at any point since the second world war and caused what scientists suspect is the country’s first firestorm thundercloud. The smoke from France’s biggest inferno in nearly 80 years choked Limoges, a city 125 miles (200km) from the flames, with more toxic dust than Delhi residents inhaled on the city’s worst day of smog last year. The blaze that tore through forests outside Bordeaux in late July took just a few weeks to reforge France’s relationship with fire, but the conditions behind it were centuries in the making. Continue reading...

data.title: Finland tried to end homelessness. What can we learn from its runaway success – and recent failures?
data.description: The Housing First policy led to the number of homeless people in Finland dropping by half. Those with firsthand experience explain why it worked At 3.30am, Vello Senkel awoke to a knock on his door. Standing on his doorstep were his neighbours with an urgent request: “Do you have salt? We want to boil macaroni.” He acquiesced, but it turned out that salt wasn’t the only ingredient they were missing: “And do you also have macaroni?” His warm face, framed by jaw-length white hair, is at once charmed and outraged as he recounts the interaction while smoking a cigarette outside his apartment building the following morning. Senkel, whose nickname is Velho (Finnish for wizard), is known for his proficiency in the kitchen. In his apartment, where he lives alongside 77 other formerly homeless people in a Helsinki suburb, he shows me his fully stocked freezer. From his neatly organised fridge he pulls out the jars of pickled cabbage and shrimp salad he has prepared to take to a friend’s house for lunch later. Continue reading...

data.title: Ceferin brands Infantino’s failed World Cup plan as ‘even worse than the Super League’
data.description: Fifa president will face opponent if he seeks re-election Ceferin: ‘We stopped another try to steal the sport’ The Uefa president, Aleksander Ceferin, has described Gianni Infantino’s doomed attempt to sell stakes in the World Cup as “even worse than the Super League plan” and warned his embattled Fifa counterpart that he will face an opponent if he runs for re-election next March. Ceferin has led Uefa’s firm collective stance against the Fifa Forward Enterprise (FFE) scheme, which was shelved amid widespread opposition at the start of August. Uefa are pushing for Infantino to quit, also drawing on support from Concacaf and the Asian Football Confederation, and are yet to drop a threat to boycott Fifa competitions while talks are under way with Concacaf to set up a combined Nations League tournament . data.description: Press Association given list of 65 items from publicly owned collection that have gone missing since 2024 A photograph of Benjamin Disraeli, an engraved portrait of William Wilberforce and a cartoon of Barbara Castle have all been misplaced by the UK parliamentary authorities, a freedom of information (FoI) request has revealed. They also include a photograph of Margaret Beckett, the UK’s first female foreign secretary and the first woman to lead Labour , and a satirical cartoon by Martin Rowson from the Conservative leadership battle of 1995. data.title: Start your engines! Trump completes fast and furious takeover of Washington with IndyCar race
data.description: US president, pushing on with Freedom 250 festivities, makes over nation’s capital for Trump rally on wheels Kyle Kirkwood wins Freedom 250 IndyCar race after Trump waves the green flag He got the wrong end of the stick. Donald Trump couldn’t figure out how to hold the green flag until his wife, Melania Trump, and Command Sgt Maj Matt Williams set him right. Then the US president waved the flag fast and furious like an excited schoolboy. The race was under way – and his conquest of Washington DC was complete. Since returning to Washington, Trump has deployed the national guard, wrecked the Lincoln Memorial reflecting pool, demolished the East Wing of the White House and run the John F Kennedy Center for the Performing Arts into the ground. His face adorns the Department of Justice, and he still has grand plans for a triumphal arch worthy of a Roman emperor. Continue reading...

data.title: ‘In 1984, I worked 363 days’: how Russ Abbot soared to success – then walked away
data.description: The comedian dominated Saturday night TV in the 1980s, with his sketch shows attracting 18 million viewers. Next came the West End musicals and sitcoms. But in 2016 he quietly disappeared from the limelight. What happened? The electronic gates slide open to reveal a gorgeous Portuguese villa, a swimming pool and a beansprout of a man. “You’ve made me feel very important,” says Russ Abbot with a smile. “Come in!” It’s more than 30 years since Abbot, aged 78, dominated Saturday night TV with his sketches, songs and impersonations. He appealed to all sorts. Kids, parents and grandparents united around the TV – first for Russ Abbot’s Madhouse, which ran from 1980 to 1985, then The Russ Abbot Show, from 1986 to 1991. He was joined by the inimitable Bella Emberg and a cast of young comics, including Les Dennis, Dustin Gee and Michael Barrymore. But make no mistake, it was Abbot’s show and the 80s was his decade. At his peak, he attracted 18 million viewers an episode. Continue reading...

data.title: Dan Tiernan: Quartz and All review – a furious comedy show about healing crystals
data.description: Monkey Barrel Comedy, Edinburgh The frenetic Mancunian turns to quartz in search of inner peace – but his standup remains as crude and self-loathing as ever I’ve seen two prominent comedians on this year’s fringe argue that your belief system is something you choose. Sign of the strange times, or just a way to justify some far-out comedy? Dan Tiernan’s show is certainly an extreme experience, as he discusses his interest – his faith, supposedly – in healing crystals. Rose quartz for calm, black tourmaline for grounding. Hard not to remark that neither seems to be doing its job well. Tiernan is the least calm and grounded comedian imaginable. You have to strap in for the ride at the Mancunian’s shows, and Quartz and All is no less so than its predecessors . It opens with Tiernan seething with his usual self-loathing, and cracking a fantastic gag about getting glasses. Now 30, he’s still ambivalent, bordering on hostile, about his sexuality and appearance: the healing crystals are a last resort, he argues, because only magic can redeem a man as freakish and unlovable as he. Such arguments are his prerogative, and he brings his woebegone plight (so lonely, he’s “getting on boats just so someone will wave at me”) to often hilarious, blood-vessel-busting life. But in the shadow of Hannah Gadsby’s Nanette , that brand of internalised-bully comedy can be uneasy viewing. Continue reading...

data.title: ‘I didn’t miss a thing’: How Nick Haymes photographed his sons’ entire lives from verrucas to homemade hamster coffin
data.description: Bloody noses, ear cleanings, the first sproutings of armpit hair … the photographer reveals how he captured his two babies growing into boys and then men Not many family photo albums open with images of the twin towers on fire. But for Nick Haymes, it made perfect sense. “When 9/11 happened,” he says, “I realised life was very short.” At the time, he was living in New York, trying to forge a career, while his friend, colleague and future wife Lina was dealing with the fallout of her previous marriage. “It made us realise we should probably get together and have a family. It was this huge historical event, but on a very micro level, it also shaped my relationship with my wife and children.” Chronograph is a photography book that runs from those terrorist attacks to the present day, tracing the journey of Haymes’s two sons, Philipp and Lawrence, as they grow from drooling babies into young men. We are given a ringside seat as arms get broken, beloved pets die and hairs start sprouting from armpits. The mundane side of life – verrucas, messy kitchens, Lina cleaning out an ear with a cotton bud – is captured in the same way as birthday parties and rites of passage. Continue reading...

data.title: Anger over slow pace of reconstruction in Italian town devastated by earthquake in 2016
data.description: As of April, two-thirds of planned public projects in Amatrice had yet to begin, rising to seven in 10 in hardest-hit areas As people gather in Amatrice on Monday for a mass to mark the 10th anniversary of the earthquake that struck the hilltop town and several neighbouring communities, killing 303 and leaving thousands homeless, politicians and other public figures will pay tribute. But for many, their words will offer little comfort: 10 years on, much of Amatrice, whose historic centre was wiped out by the 6.0 magnitude quake, is still being rebuilt and more than half of its roughly 2,100 residents continue to live in temporary housing. data.title: The Terror: Devil in Silver review – this psychiatric hospital horror is scary on so many levels
data.description: Expect gory set pieces and jump scares galore in the return of the supernatural anthology series, with Dan Stevens among the many poor souls terrorised by an evil spirit haunting their ward Things that go bump in the night? Bad. Things that go bump in the night in a dilapidated psychiatric hospital? Infinitely worse. That, basically, is the premise of Devil in Silver, the latest volume of anthology series The Terror, which began in 2018 with a supernaturally charged tale of a polar expedition to find out what happened to Sir John Franklin’s voyage. Crikey, it does not end well. The next was set during the second world war and was about shapeshifters from Japanese folklore terrorising a Japanese-American community in southern California. A hiatus followed, but now The Terror is back with a double dose of horror: a malevolent spirit moving in and out of the bodies of the patients of New Hyde psychiatric hospital, and the more tangible but no less frightening diabolism of the US mental healthcare system. Pepper (Dan Stevens, still of Downton Abbey fame despite his many varied roles since) is in New Hyde because the three policemen who arrested him after they caught a few punches he was aiming at his girlfriend’s controlling ex threw him in there rather than completing the paperwork the station would have required. There he meets the lost and suffering souls who have ended up in what amounts, due to underfunding and understaffing, to a holding pen rather than a rehabilitative or care facility. Dorry (Judith Light) is the longest-serving resident – put there decades ago by her husband because of her endless crying fits, though her later memories reveal a greater darkness. Kofi (Chinaza Uche) – or Coffee, as he is called by the rest of his companions until it is too late – was a structural engineer in Ghana but now depends on medication to keep himself steady. Loochie (played by non-binary actor b) ended up in the system after a violent incident with a sibling, but at least one member of staff believes her charge is able to cope in the real world and, as the hospital’s evil spirit gathers strength and wrath, gets the chance to prove it. Continue reading...

data.title: Marine Le Pen's career has been resurrected – and she is a bigger threat than ever | Mujtaba Rahman
data.description: No longer banned from next year’s presidential election, Le Pen is a far more formidable force than her understudy, Jordan Bardella France loves a battle-scarred survivor. Charles de Gaulle, François Mitterrand and Jacques Chirac clawed their way back from political failure to become presidents of the republic. There is a significant chance that Marine Le Pen will be next. Now that the Paris appeal court has unshackled her from an electoral ban for fraud, the far-right veteran has double appeal in the race for the French presidency next year. She will run, as always, as an outsider and a scourge of the political elites – despite continuously holding electoral office since 1998. She can also now pose as a “miraculous survivor”, a “mother courage” and “a battling granny”, as senior French political figures, including former ministers, described her to me during recent conversations in Paris. Mujtaba Rahman is the managing director for Europe at Eurasia Group, a political risk research and consulting firm Continue reading...

data.title: The PM is promising to fix our everyday annoyances – and I have a list to get him started | Emma Beddington
data.description: Andy Burnham hopes we’ll forget the big stuff if he sorts out our minor frustrations and low-level gripes. Pothole politics hasn’t won me over yet, but I know some changes that could This is a vulnerable confession, but I spend way too much time on the social media of the New York City mayor, Zohran Mamdani. Whether he is seemingly effortlessly speaking Mandarin, hanging out with kids or charmingly accepting that he should wear a cycle helmet, the man with the million-watt smile is my antidepressant. (Even more vulnerable confession: I believe, irrationally, he is looking after my elder son, who lives there.) This means that I know all about Mamdani’s fight against what Business Insider recently deemed the “annoyance economy” – daily frustrations that make you poorer or drive you slowly, miserably mad. These include the absurd complexity of cancelling subscriptions; hidden fees; getting charged more for something you looked up last week, because of cookies; never being able to find a public toilet; and potholes. He has taken to responding when he gets tagged in people’s “Mamdani, fix this” posts to the point where Britons online are even jokily asking him to take on their problems. Continue reading...

data.title: Walking the Peak District, I discovered a wonderful rejection of the right’s monotone vision of England | John Harris
data.description: The landscape was striking, but so was the diversity of the hikers. We can make this the new normal – and we should A fortnight or so ago, my two teenage kids and I set out on a three-night visit to the Peak District where temperatures were hovering at a comparatively tepid 28C. We stayed at a youth hostel – more of which in a moment – and began the trip with the 20-minute ascent of Mam Tor , a modest peak that pulls in both dedicated ramblers who then yomp along the ridge beyond, and newbies who mostly want to get to the top and immerse themselves in the jaw-dropping view. The next bit might sound self-parodically Guardian-esque, but what the hell: in its own way, the most striking sight was the diversity of the scores of people rambling up, down and along. Women in their 20s wearing hijabs picnicked on giant rocks, while multiracial gaggles of young men attempted to race to the top; solo and shirtless white fitness freaks and retirement-age dog walkers took their places alongside them. With plenty of justification, country walking has long been typified as one of the most monoculturally white pursuits there is. But here – presumably because of the relatively close proximity of Manchester and Sheffield – things looked different. John Harris is a Guardian columnist Continue reading...

data.title: The Guardian view on Andy Burnham’s foreign policy: work in progress | Editorial
data.description: The prime minister has focused on domestic affairs since coming to office. But at a time of global disruption, he will need to define Britain’s place in the world A run of volatility in domestic British politics in recent years has tracked a period of global turbulence, and yet foreign policy over the same period has been an area of relative stability. What little is known about Andy Burnham’s approach to international relations expresses more continuity with Sir Keir Starmer’s administration than deviation. In negotiations with the EU, the red lines that prohibit membership of the single market or customs union still stand . Where Washington is concerned, Mr Burnham shows no interest in performances of bonhomie with Donald Trump, but his predecessor had already swapped that approach for a cooler pragmatic tone by the end of his tenure. The new foreign secretary, Ed Miliband, has opened a good dialogue with Marco Rubio , his US counterpart. Such is the density of integration in defence and security matters that incoming UK prime ministers, regardless of ideology, have little choice but to invest time in cultivating a bond with whoever sits in the White House. Anyone hoping for a spectacular transatlantic rupture and sudden clinch with Brussels will be disappointed. Continue reading...

data.title: The Guardian view on the new Hungary: de-Orbánising at pace | Editorial
data.description: As a Brussels deadline looms with over €10bn at stake, Péter Magyar’s first three months have been transformative in addressing a corrupt legacy Some elections are more important than others. Since taking office in May, Hungary’s new prime minister, Péter Magyar, has embarked upon the country’s most far-reaching and dramatic programme of transformation since the fall of communism in 1989. Mr Magyar’s predecessor, Viktor Orbán, established a soft autocracy which thrived on corruption and, over 16 years, exerted its grip on most areas of Hungarian life, from religion to culture and the media. It is being dismantled at extraordinary pace. Last week, a newly appointed president took office following the sacking of Tamás Sulyok, accused by Mr Magyar of having rubber-stamped the erosion of the rule of law in the country. In stark contrast, András Baka is a former president of Hungary’s supreme court, a role he was removed from by the Orbán regime in an action judged unlawful by the European court of human rights. Continue reading...

data.title: Frustrated Lewis Hamilton claims Ferrari strategy cost him F1 Dutch GP podium
data.description: Briton says team too slow to pit Charles Leclerc ‘It’s something that we need to discuss offline’ Lewis Hamilton has told his Ferrari team that they must up their game if he is to remain in the Formula One world championship fight after the British driver was angry with strategy calls at the Dutch Grand Prix , comparing them unfavourably with the decisive way his former team ­Mercedes had acted. The race was won by McLaren’s Lando Norris from Mercedes’ Kimi Antonelli and George Russell. Hamilton was fourth but believed he might have had a shot of a podium had Ferrari moved Charles Leclerc aside sooner when Hamilton, on a different tyre strategy, was quicker than his teammate. data.title: ‘Call his agent’: Emery feels Watkins should explain absence from Villa’s rout by Brighton
data.description: England forward is considering move to Al-Hilal ‘This question is for him … I answer only with silence’ Unai Emery did nothing to deny that Ollie Watkins had refused to play for Aston Villa in their sobering 4-0 defeat by Brighton at the Amex on Sunday. The head coach had a selection crisis up front with Brian Madjo and Tammy Abraham injured. However, he did not include Watkins in the matchday squad as the England striker considers a move to Al-Hilal in Saudi Arabia. Emery was forced to rely on the attacking midfielder Emiliano Buendía as an emergency striker and his team disappeared without trace on the south coast. They were 4-0 down after 31 minutes and had their new signing João Gomes sent off on his debut in the 40th minute. Gomes kicked up and out at the Brighton striker Georginio Rutter after being dispossessed by him. Continue reading...

data.title: Arthur Fils wins first Masters title after beating Frances Tiafoe in Cincinnati final
data.description: 22-year-old wins 6-3, 1-6, 6-0 Fils now ranked No 11 in world Arthur Fils has always believed he was on the path to the very top of his chosen sport. Even when others considered him too young, too green or far too self-confident, he has entered the biggest tournaments in the world with the intention of winning them, ambitions he did not hesitate to express. On a historic afternoon in Mason, Ohio, Fils took an huge step forward in pursuit of those massive goals as the 22-year-old became a Masters 1000 champion for the first time in his young career. His greatest achievement was secured with a supreme mental effort under pressure as the Frenchman dragged himself back into contention after a desperate second set, recovering to defeat Frances Tiafoe 6-3, 1-6, 6-0 and win the Cincinnati Open. On a historic afternoon in Mason, Ohio, Fils took an huge step forward in pursuit of those massive goals as the 22-year-old became a Masters 1000 champion for the first time in his young career. His greatest achievement was secured with a supreme mental effort under pressure as the Frenchman dragged himself back into contention after a desperate second set, recovering to defeat Frances Tiafoe 6-3, 1-6, 6-0 and win the Cincinnati Open. data.title: Le Court claims Tour of Britain glory despite Wiebes’s fourth stage win in five
data.description: Mauritian claims landmark victory at Leamington Spa Wiebes finishes second after 137th career stage win Kim Le Court sealed overall victory in the Tour of Britain Women in Royal Leamington Spa, as Lorena Wiebes took her fourth sprint win in this year’s race and the 11th stage victory of her career. Wiebes has surpassed Mark Cavendish’s career mark of 10 stage wins and now has the most victories of any rider competing in either the men’s or women’s Tour of Britain. Le Court, who won a stage and finished ninth overall in the Tour de France Femmes earlier this month, based her success on a solo victory in Friday’s uphill finish to the Great Orme, overlooking Llandudno. It was the most significant race victory of the Mauritian rider’s career. Continue reading...

data.title: Mateta’s Palace dispute deepens after losing appeals to end contract early
data.description: Striker wants move and said final year of deal was invalid 29-year-old took his case to tribunal and Fifa but lost Jean-Philippe Mateta is in dispute with Crystal Palace over the final year of his contract but failed in an attempt to have it ruled invalid by an independent Premier League tribunal and Fifa. The France striker signed a four-and-a-half-year contract when he joined permanently from Mainz in January 2022 after an initial loan, in a deal that also included the option of a 12-month extension. That was activated by Palace in 2024, with Mateta’s contract now due to expire at the end of this season. But it is understood the 29-year-old and his representatives have disputed whether that extension was valid and took the case to an independent tribunal under Premier League regulations last season. Official confirmation of the outcome has not been disclosed, although Palace insist Mateta’s contract remains binding and he played in their defeat at Everton on Saturday. Fifa also rejected his claim after ruling it did not have jurisdiction over the dispute. Mateta’s representative has been approached for comment. Continue reading...

data.title: ‘I love it. It’s hope’: the mysterious self-willed wildflower meadow that seeded itself
data.description: Farmer Derek Sayer let a boggy field run wild and just one annual hay-cut has led to remarkable biodiversity Tucked away on a country lane, a small field bursts with yellow and pink flowers. Quail and whitethroats call from the thick hedges and the plants, including common centaury, yellow rattle and marsh and common spotted orchids, bounce with hoverflies and butterflies. More than 150 plant species have been recorded on Sayer’s Old Meadow, in north Norfolk, England, which is remarkable when there was just one – oilseed rape – growing there 21 years ago. data.title: ‘So many people say things about my appearance – it’s not normal’: Jorja Smith on burnout, body-shaming and finding freedom
data.description: Being recognised by the Brits, Grammys and Drake made the singer one of British music’s most famous names – and also left her exhausted. Now, after decompressing in her home town she returns with a record made for raving It is a sticky, sweltering July afternoon, and I have accidentally found myself at a wake with Jorja Smith. I’m told that the pub where we have met, in the leafiest part of leafy south-west London, is usually a safe bet for an inconspicuous table. But today, sweaty black suits carrying pints drift between tables, and long queues snake round the bar. Dressed in a simple tank top, bare-faced with her hair scraped back, Smith is waiting for me when I arrive. “I’ve been waiting for my drink for ages,” she says. “But I feel bad saying anything because, you know …” Continue reading...

data.title: ‘The country of my birth has lost its heart’: Miriam Margolyes on how to fix broken Britain
data.description: At 85, the actor has lived through much political upheaval. But, she writes, today’s hostile times feel like ‘the worst yet’. She reflects on her journey from teenage Tory to full-throated leftist – and says there’s still time to save the nation from the bad guys A funny thing happened on the way to 2026: I got old and the world turned nasty. It happened very quickly and it’s to do with politics (the world) and pelvic floor weakness (mine). It’s strange being this old. Sometimes when I look in the mirror, it’s a shock to see wrinkles and grey hair, because inside I am still that naughty Oxford High School girl, risking detention just for the joy of entertaining her friends. People assume that with great age comes great wisdom, but actually we remain who we have always been, only more so, and we need to make our peace with that and with each other. The Britain I grew up in, though – that feels almost unrecognisable, and everyone I speak to says the same thing. The historian Eric Hobsbawm, whom I knew and loved, argued that people invent the past they want for their own purposes – that the real past was quite different: “Today is the great age of historical mythology.” He’s right, but that past is still the safe haven I’d like to return to. People feel adrift, they don’t understand or feel a connection to the place they thought they knew. Continue reading...

data.title: Bebe Cave: Swoon review – dazzling portrait of marginalised muses and the male gaze
data.description: Pleasance Dome, Edinburgh Smart, slapstick and silly, this chaotic multicharacter comedy sends up the Pre-Raphaelite Brotherhood Some of the most revered works of art across history feature women as their primary focus. But though they might appear as favoured subjects, so often these women are relegated to the margins, their stories untold as they remain silent and often sexualised via the male gaze. In her new multicharacter comedy Swoon, Bebe Cave interrogates the role of the muse and what it means to be seen yet never heard. We initially meet Cave as Elizabeth Siddal – or Lizzie – who was immortalised as Ophelia by John Everett Millais in the mid 19th century, also becoming a popular model for several other pre-Raphaelite artists. data.title: A supreme being, the nearly naked show and politics with paws: Edinburgh fringe pick’n’mix
data.description: From Taiwanese steampunk dance to Australian climate comedy, here are 13 quick-fire fringe reviews All our Edinburgh festival reviews For new perspective on the strange ways we behave, we all know the thought experiment “if a visitor from space arrived on Earth, what would they think?” In Born Sexy Yesterday, Anna Leong Brophy plays a supreme being implanted into a grown woman’s body to experience life for the first time. Presenting like some sci-fi sex robot with the soul of a naive child, Brophy duly marries a man on the front row and settles down to a life of domestic drudgery. Until she discovers she has other settings, other brands of femininity available for her to try out … Thus begins a potent hour, not always hilarious but undeniably persuasive, protesting against the strictly circumscribed roles that women are allowed to play – particularly in the movies, as Brophy sardonically demonstrates. data.title: ‘I was scared I was going mad’: Meg Mason speaks to fellow authors about the parasocial relationships that begin on the page
data.description: As a lonely teenager, the novels of Nancy Mitford offered the Sorrow and Bliss author a lifeline - and an imaginary friend. She explores why reading can create a particularly intense bond with a favourite writer In the summer before university, my mother gave me a copy of The Pursuit of Love . We’d moved countries at the beginning of my A-levels and those months in between had been defined by a level of loneliness I had never known in my life. The sort of loneliness so acute and pervasive it feels like panic, and on top of all that, so shaming to be 17 with nowhere to go and nothing to do on a Saturday night. Growing up, my mother – a great reader – would say: “When you’ve got a book, you’ve got a friend,” which is why, presumably, I wasn’t a great reader. Then, I’d always had actual friends. And suddenly I didn’t and presumably that is why I accepted the Nancy Mitford paperback and started to read it. Continue reading...

data.title: As You Like It review – French aristocratic trappings bring fresh comedy to Arden
data.description: Shakespeare’s Globe, London In a lively and deftly designed production, gowns and wigs fit for Versailles give way to plainer disguises as banished courtiers pursue happiness in the country For a play that pivots around the liberating disguises inside Arden’s bucolia, this production of the Bard’s pastoral comedy begins the dress-up long before its characters enter the forest for their games on gender and identity. Duke Frederick’s court resembles that of Louis XVI’s Versailles, with flamboyant gesticulations that seem to belong to Molière. It is Shakespeare, but it could be a French period romp. Costumes become plainer and more earthy in Arden. Is there a suggestion that these characters live their courtly lives in a constant state of disguise? Continue reading...

data.title: Chineke!/ Heyward/ Angel Blue review – belated premiere for forgotten Black composer
data.description: Royal Albert Hall, London A suite of reconstructed dance pieces from 1918 by Edmund Thornton Jenkins made a moving start to Chineke!’s Prom, where soprano Angel Blue sang Barber’s nostalgic Knoxville and Dvořák’s Symphony No 8 made a breathless finale Slowly but surely, our perceptions of what a composer looked like in the early 20th century are widening. Chineke! ’s ongoing mission to unearth music by forgotten Black composers here brought about the belated premiere of Ballet by Edmund Thornton Jenkins, its incomplete manuscript parts reconstructed by his great-nephew Tuffus Zimbabwe . Growing up in Charleston, South Carolina, Jenkins died in Paris aged only 32, having made a name for himself as a rising composer and band leader. In between he studied at the Royal Academy of Music in London, where in 1918 he wrote his three-movement Ballet. It sounded persuasive here, as conducted by Jonathon Heyward. A substantial opening Processional, ominous then light-footed, gives way to a second movement beginning with a bubbling flute duet and a florid viola solo; together, these repeatedly show a gift for weaving together melody and countermelody. The flaw is in the finale, where the waltz that dominates the movement sounds unavoidably slender and staid next to the trumpet fanfare that announces it. Still, Jenkins rounds things off with an exuberant, uptempo ending. Continue reading...

data.title: The new Halloween video game has been banned in Australia – and not because of the violence
data.description: Academics and a former classification board director say Halloween: The Game’s ban due to ‘incentivised drug use’ highlights an incoherent set of standards Get our breaking news email , free app or daily news podcast Halloween’s Michael Myers is one of film’s most feared boogeymen, responsible for some of the most brutal on-screen deaths in horror cinema. The US video game developer Illfonic looked to reproduce those terrors in its upcoming title Halloween: The Game, with gruesome killings a major focus of the gameplay: for instance, you can stomp another player’s head through a toilet seat, or fry their brain by throwing them through a television screen. But Australians will not be able to play Halloween, because it has been refused classification by the Australian Classification Board, which means it is banned from sale within the country. And it’s not because of the violence or murders. Continue reading...

data.title: Aardman’​s Peter Lord and David Sproxton: ‘At the Oscars, I went to the gents and had a pee with Jack Nicholson!’
data.description: The ​s​tudio’s co-founders on ​accidentally creating Morph, not wanting a yacht in the Maldives and being each other’s best ally Peter Lord and David Sproxton are the founders of Aardman Animations. The pair began animating as teenagers, selling their first short – starring a superhero called Aardman – to the BBC’s Vision On in 1972. In 1977, they created Morph for the children’s programme Take Hart. The studio’s breakthrough into adult audiences came via Channel 4’s Conversation Pieces series, and its animators, including a young Nick Park, went on to make Wallace & Gromit, whose films have won multiple Academy Awards. Aardman became employee-owned in 2018, with Lord and Sproxton transferring majority ownership to staff to safeguard the company’s independence. They were knighted earlier this year. data.title: Café Clement, London WC2: ‘Turns out it’s really rather good’ – restaurant review
data.description: I am forever curious as to how these kind of sizzling places feel on a normal Tuesday two months in, especially when the celebrities are all off sunning their bottoms in Tuscany Café Clement , the all-day restaurant inside Nick Jones’ new St Clement Hotel at 180 The Thames in central London, opened with a bang in June and immediately rocketed to the top of every “sell your grandmother for a terrace table” list in London. Which isn’t that much of a surprise, seeing as Jones, founder of Soho House , is the master of restaurant rumpus. Within days, Stanley Tucci , Nick Grimshaw and full-length-trouser-phobic heart-throb Paul Mescal were all there, tucking into oeufs mayonnaise and lobster omelettes while politely ignoring the fact that the place was still, in many ways, a building site. The hotel itself isn’t due to open fully until early autumn, when a rooftop restaurant, Lunette , will also arrive with some of London’s most wondrous views and Florence Knight at the helm. Still, Café Clement opened to frothy praise, and I am forever curious as to how these kind of sizzling places feel on a normal Tuesday two months in, when the celebrities are all off sunning their bottoms in Tuscany and, frankly, lunch is not free. Continue reading...

data.title: How to make the perfect zaru soba, or cold soba noodles – recipe | Felicity Cloake's How to make the perfect
data.description: Hot days call for cool dinners, and these are Japan’s nutty, salty and sweet solution. Fiery or pickled accompaniments optional Although every culture craves something different in hot weather – chilled beetroot soup in Lithuania, cooling buttermilk drinks in India, gazpacho in Spain – what many of these dishes have in common is a certain soothing silkiness as they slide down the throat, plus a decent helping of salt. Japan’s zaru soba , which Namiko Hirasawa Chen of Just One Cookbook describes as her family’s “go-to meal when the summer heat and humidity soar”, is no exception. Cold, slippery noodles paired with a savoury dipping sauce, it’s a simple, satisfying dish that’s ready in 15 minutes, and can be accessorised with crunchy salads, sweet seafood or creamy tofu sides for something more substantial. Traditionally served on a bamboo mat, or zaru , to allow the noodles to drain, you can get away without one at home (though lose the seaweed and you can call it mori soba instead), this is definitely one to stick in your summer repertoire alongside the chilled soups, watermelon salads and cucumber sandwiches. Continue reading...

data.title: Quench your thirst! 20 perfect spritzes and shandies to try now – from kumquat to portergaff
data.description: Whether you love a traditional spritz or tend towards a wilder libation, this August there are bubbly and sophisticated drinks to suit every taste This summer, UK web searches for “Hugo spritz”, an elderflower-flavoured aperitif, overtook searches for “Aperol spritz” for the first time. As the spritz craze shows no sign of slowing down, pub chains are taking wild liberties, calling anything fizzy and served in a large glass over ice a spritz – and charging £10-plus for it. Echo Falls blue raspberry spritz? Pink gin spritz (Slug & Lettuce)? Raspberry vodka and honey spritz (Young’s)? Malibu cranberry spritz (Stonegate)? Mamma mia ! Traditionally, the spritz is an Italian cocktail made from prosecco, a bitter aperitif or liqueur, and a splash of soda water to keep things steady. While Venetian bartenders are more likely to judge it by eye, there is a simple 3-2-1 formula for making a spritz at home: three parts prosecco, two parts liqueur and one part soda water. I’ve gone with 75ml/50ml/25ml – keep the same ratios to make a smaller (60ml/40ml/20ml) or larger (90ml/60ml/30ml) drink. Of course, you can then adjust it to make it stronger or weaker (I have been known to leave out the soda …). Continue reading...

data.title: Drill, Burnham, drill? The oil basin that is a totem for Trump – and a headache for Britain’s new PM
data.description: North Sea oil, once the driving force of the UK economy, may be dwindling but it remains a symbol of prestige and a rich resource for political debate When oil was first discovered off the north-east coast of Scotland in September 1969, industry folklore has it that the duty superintendent on the rig carefully poured it into a pickle jar commandeered from the canteen and took it back to Amoco’s Great Yarmouth office in Norfolk. There, it was emptied into an ash tray, sniffed and then set alight. From that modest start, North Sea oil – as the huge basin of oil and gas reserves quickly became known – emerged as a driving force of the British economy and a symbol of national power and renewal as the UK emerged from the Opec oil crisis. Continue reading...

CNN on Saturday reported that a deactivated account which Harp had on what is now known as X was packed with fiercely pro-Trump messages on the day of the January 6 Capitol attack in Washington DC, including posts repeating his lies that the 2020 election, which he lost to Joe Biden toward the end of his first presidency, had been stolen from by fraudsters. data.title: Democrats incredulous over Hakeem Jeffries and Jared Kushner meeting
data.description: Critics include Senator Chris van Hollen, ex-aide to Obama Tommy Vietor and ex-Republican congressman Adam Kinzinger Democrats and other Donald Trump critics reacted incredulously to a New York Times report on Sunday that House Democratic leader Hakeem Jeffries met with Jared Kushner, the president’s influential son-in-law, to discuss possible areas of collaboration. The reported meeting comes months ahead of the November midterm elections in which Democrats are favored to retake the US House, a development that would make Jeffries speaker. If they are in the majority, Democrats are expected to use their oversight power to aggressively investigate the Trump administration, including self-enrichment by the president and his family. data.title: The lesson from Canada’s collapsed trade talks with the US: negotiation may be futile
data.description: Breakdown shows Washington now prioritises its own interests over any semblance of shared economic ground ‘No more!!!’: Trump lashes out after US-Canada talks devolve into trade war The calamitous collapse of trade negotiations between Canada and the United States is a warning to nations worldwide that pursuing any kind of dialogue with the current US administration is doomed at the outset, according to observers who say this recent episode indicates seeking a fair deal is futile. Andrea Lawlor, an associate professor of political science at McMaster University in Ontario, said: “No matter the closeness of the historical relationship, the American administration has signalled that it now prioritises its interests above those of some sort of global economic coordination or harmony. Continue reading...

Inför finalen var det otroligt tajt i toppen, och det fanns inte utrymme för några misstag. Schweizaren Steve Guerdat var iskall, och säkrade guldet med två nollor.

data.title: Fredrik skjutsade skadad pojke i sin epa: ”Såg när han blev huggen”

data.title: W Rosji płoną magazyny firmy Ozon. USA i Iran wymieniają się groźbami

data.title: Babiš s Macinkou přijmou české velvyslance. Řešit budou i bezpečnost
data.description: V pondělí ráno přijme ministr zahraničních věcí Petr Macinka (Motoristé) a premiér Andrej Babiš (ANO) v Černínském paláci v Praze vedoucí českých zastupitelských úřadů. data.title: Vývoj amerických léků se bez Číny neobejde. Politici varují před závislostí na Pekingu
data.description: Americké farmaceutické firmy stále častěji poohlížejí po nových lécích v Číně. Tamní společnosti je totiž často dokážou vyvíjet rychleji a hlavně levněji. data.title: Potravinové doplňky mohou ohrozit zdraví. Až třetina zkontrolovaných je závadná
data.description: Užívání bylin ve formě čajů, tinktur nebo jako součást některých potravinových doplňků může podpořit léčbu i ozdravné procesy v těle. Nadužívání nebo nevhodné kombinace přírodních látek ale mohou způsobit vážné zdravotní potíže. Zejména u některých produktů z dovozu člověk navíc často kupuje „zajíce v pytli“, protože v nich může být příměs nepovolených, neúčinných, či dokonce toxických látek.

data.title: Požár umakartového jádra zdevastoval byt v Praze. Hasiči zachránili pět lidí
data.description: Na pražském Chodově dnes večer hořelo bytové jádro. Hasiči z domu evakuovali osm lidí a pět jich zachránili a předali do péče zdravotnických záchranářů. Novinářům to sdělil mluvčí pražských hasičů Vojtěch Rotschedl. Záchranáři do nemocnice odvezli jednoho člověka, který se nadýchal zplodin hoření, řekl jejich mluvčí Karel Kirs.

data.title: Drony Peklo a Paljanycja zničily ruskou flotilu. Čím Ukrajina udeřila na přístav?
data.description: Ukrajina při útoku na ruskou námořní základnu v Novorossijsku poprvé nasadila v jediné operaci čtyři typy raketových dronů. data.title: Staronový vítěz spořádal 193 knedlíků. Soutěž se konala při festivalu Trnkobraní
data.description: Soutěž v pojídání švestkových knedlíků, které je spojené s vizovickým hudebním festivalem Trnkobraní, začíná být poněkud fádní. Alespoň pokud jde o jejího vítěze. Letos se jím totiž už posedmé v řadě stal Radim Dvořáček z Ostravy, který během hodiny spořádal 193 švestkových knedlíků. Jeden váží 30 gramů a jde o velice tence obalenou švestku.

data.title: VIDEA TÝDNE: Turkovo házení jogurtů, smrt na přejezdu a robot rychlejší než Bolt
data.description: Arnold Schwarzenegger musí být pyšný. Akumulátorová vrtačka z Lidlu rozpohybovala Londýnské oko a zapsala se do Guinnessovy knihy rekordů. Hazard se životem s tragickým koncem zachytila kamera na přejezdu v Rájci-Jestřebí na Blanensku. Robot od Unitree překonal rekord Usaina Bolta, v Portlandu se dvě kozy vydaly na cestu autobusem a Filip Turek na sebe opět upozornil. Tentokrát videem s házením jogurtů.

data.title: Jeden z nejtragičtějších víkendů roku. Nehody na silnicích nepřežilo sedm lidí
data.description: O nynějším víkendu na českých silnicích zemřelo už sedm lidí. Jde tak o jeden z nejtragičtějších víkendů tohoto roku. V sobotu si nehody vyžádaly pět obětí, v neděli již dvě. Vyplývá to z informací policie. Podobně tragický byl i víkend před dvěma týdny, kdy od pátku do neděle zemřelo na silnicích osm lidí. Stejný počet obětí zaznamenala policie i o víkendu na přelomu července a srpna.

data.title: Uhynul z lidské blbosti, smutní po ztrátě lachtana v Liberci. Nejde o první případ
data.description: Podezřelý klid panuje v neděli u venkovního bazénu lachtanů v liberecké zoo. Kde jindy výskají děti a šplouchá voda, je ticho, které ruší jen občasné zapraskání z reproduktorů. Návštěvníci nahlížejí do vody a hledají lachtana Huga. Marně. V noci na sobotu uhynul poté, co rozkousal dětskou panenku a pozřel její hlavičku. Chovatelé mu už nemohli pomoci. Není to přitom poprvé, kdy lachtan v Liberci uhynul kvůli nezodpovědným návštěvníkům.

data.title: Těžce zranil ženu, transportoval ji vrtulník. Policie nakonec útočníka dopadla

data.title: Apatická a podvyživená zvířata. Válka je traumatizuje, říká majitel zoo v Gaze
data.description: Když děti vešly do zoo poblíž uprchlického tábora Nusajrát v Gaze, spatřily lva, který se na ně sotva ohlédl skrz mříže své klece, a šimpanze sedící apaticky ve výběhu. Řada zvířat byla podvyživená a oslabená kvůli nedostatku potravy, léků a vakcín. Stále však byla naživu, a to díky majiteli zoo Mahmúdu Džumaovi.

data.title: Čína pokračuje v Česku v kyberšpionáži, měli bychom mít plán B, uvedl šéf NÚKIB
data.description: V Česku pokračují pokusy o čínskou kyberšpionáž, řekl šéf Národního úřadu pro kybernetickou a informační bezpečnost (NÚKIB) Lukáš Kintr v pořadu Poledne s Moravcem. Stát by měl být podle Kintra opatrný ohledně posilování své závislosti na čínských technologiích a měl by mít připravený centrální "plán B" pro případ, že by tyto technologie přestaly fungovat.

data.title: „Maso“, „služebka“ a „vynulovat“. Slang dovoluje Rusům mluvit o válce na Ukrajině
data.description: Nový vojenský slang umožňuje ruským vojákům popsat realitu na frontě, kterou ruský režim popírá. Slova jako „vynulovat“, „služebka“ nebo „maso“ odhalují bezcitné násilí velitelů a zkorumpovanost armády. Tvrdí to sociální antropoložka Alexandra Archipová a psycholog Juril Lapšin v novém výzkumu, který přiblížil server Der Spiegel. Z 6 739 dopisů izolovali 77 nových výrazů, které se nevyužívají pouze na frontě, ale i doma.

data.title: Libya’s central bank chief resigns
data.description:
TRIPOLI: The governor of Libya’s central bank, Naji Issa, has resigned without giving a reason, several reports said on Monday.
	Private TV channel Al-Ahrar said Issa had confirmed his resignation.
	Issa and vice-governor Miree Al-Barasee were appointed by Libya’s parliament, which is based in the east of the divided country, in September 2024.
	His appointment was part of a deal backed by the United Nations that ended a standoff over Libya’s oil production and a deep financial crisis.

data.title: Trump insists Netanyahu relationship ‘very good’ despite Gaza rift
data.description:
WASHINGTON, United States: President Donald Trump insisted on Monday that his relationship with Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu is “very good” despite the Israeli leader’s rejection of a US-led Gaza plan.
	“The relationship is very good,” Trump said in response to a shouted question from a journalist at the end of an Oval Office event.
	After more than a week of gradually escalating criticism, Netanyahu explicitly stated on Sunday that he opposed the Gaza plan, which called for Israel to begin pulling back forces in tandem with disarmament by Hamas.

data.title: Final election phase begins in Pakistan-administered Kashmir despite banned group’s boycott call
data.description:

	Men and women began lining up early at polling stations in Poonch district in the disputed Himalayan region, where four assembly seats were being contested.

data.title: Can Al-Burhan’s Sudanese national dialogue turn military gains into a political settlement?
data.description:
LONDON: More than three years after Sudan descended into civil war, army chief Gen. Abdel Fattah Al-Burhan is pushing for a broad national dialogue aimed at rebuilding the country’s political institutions and laying the foundations for a civilian transition.

	Talks could begin as early as August, with preparatory consultations already involving political groups, technocrats, Sufi leaders, traditional authorities, academics, professionals, civil society representatives and independent figures.

data.title: La RN9 sous un délai de grâce
data.description: La réhabilitation de la route dite boulevard Adolphe Nshimirimana, sur certains axes liés au projet de réhabilitation du port de Bujumbura, n’a pas respecté le délai initial de 24 mois. Alors que les travaux semblent au ralenti et que des rumeurs de détournement des fonds circulent, les responsables du projet assurent que le chantier se poursuit et annoncent que le délai d’exécution a été prolongé. Ils évoquent aussi l’état de la réhabilitation du port de Bujumbura.

data.description: La concertation nationale entre dans une phase concrète à Madagascar. Après plusieurs semaines d'attente, le dispositif chargé d'accompagner le processus commence à prendre forme. data.title: Baccalauréat 2026 : le taux de réussite en hausse à Antananarivo avec 51,74 %
data.description: Les candidats au baccalauréat de la province d'Antananarivo connaissent désormais leur sort. Pour cette session 2026, 51,74 % des candidats ont décroché leur diplôme, contre 47,49 % l'année précédente. Le taux de réussite gagne ainsi 4,25 points et repasse au-dessus de la barre des 50 %. La délibération a fixé le seuil d'admission à 9,75/20. Cette progression intervient dans la province qui concentre le plus important contingent du pays, avec près de 62 000 inscrits avant les épreuves. (…) - Enseignement

data.title: Riz importé : le gouvernement fait machine arrière et suspend les nouvelles taxes
data.description: Le gouvernement malgache revoit sa copie sur la fiscalité du riz importé. Le droit de douane de 20 % et la TVA de 5 % prévus sur le riz de luxe dans la loi de finances rectificative 2026 sont temporairement suspendus. Cette décision intervient alors que l'approche de la période de soudure fait craindre des tensions sur l'approvisionnement et les prix. Le ministère du Commerce reconnaît que la production nationale demeure insuffisante pour satisfaire entièrement la demande. Ce recul place (…) - Economie

data.description: À l'issue de son 46e Sommet des chefs d'État et de gouvernement à Durban, l'organisation régionale encourage Madagascar à poursuivre sa marche vers le retour à la normalité constitutionnelle. Cet accompagnement est toutefois assorti de plusieurs recommandations portant notamment sur le fonctionnement démocratique, la redevabilité, les droits de l'Homme et la participation citoyenne. Dans son communiqué, la SADC salue également les consultations menées à Madagascar sous l'égide de son (…) - Politique

data.title: Bad Bunny cierra su gira mundial en casa: “Puerto Rico, gracias. Soy de ustedes por siempre”

data.title: ¿Cómo construyó Fernando Cerimedo un puente entre Miami y el poder político de Washington?
data.description: La investigación aporta nuevos datos sobre el argentino Fernando Cerimedo, estratega de la ultraderecha en América Latina acusado de intento de asesinado de su ex pareja en Bolivia.  No solo tiene contactos en Estados Unidos, como ha dicho la prensa, sino que su modelo de intervención política latinoamericana encontró en Miami una plataforma estable y en el consultor Damián Merlo un mecanismo profesionalizado de entrada al poder de Washington. The post ¿Cómo construyó Fernando Cerimedo un puente entre Miami y el poder político de Washington? first appeared on Cubadebate .

data.title: El 19 % de Cerimedo: la operación del golpe electoral en Honduras
data.description: El primero de diciembre de 2025, unas horas después de que se cerraran las urnas, visité un grupo de compañeros de colectivos que habían estado en mesas electorales. El relato era pasmoso y los rostros mostraban rabia y frustración. Uno de ellos me dijo: “Nunca habíamos perdido ni una sola urna de mi centro de votación, pero ayer las perdimos todas”; otro me dijo: “No podemos explicarnos qué pasó”. Ese fenómeno se repitió a lo largo y ancho del país. The post El 19 % de Cerimedo: la operación del golpe electoral en Honduras first appeared on Cubadebate .

data.title: Cardenal Rodríguez hace impactante llamado a los jóvenes hondureños
data.description: Tegucigalpa, Honduras. Durante su homilía dominical, el cardenal Óscar Andrés Rodríguez llamó a las familias a recuperar la oración y la enseñanza de la fe en el hogar, ante lo que considera una pérdida de formación religiosa entre las nuevas generaciones. El cardenal Óscar Andrés Rodríguez dirigió este domingo un mensaje especialmente a las familias y los jóvenes , a quienes instó a preguntarse qué lugar ocupa Jesús en sus vidas y a recuperar la oración como parte de la convivencia cotidiana en el hogar. A partir del pasaje del Evangelio en el que Jesús pregunta a sus discípulos “¿Quién dicen que soy yo?”, Rodríguez trasladó esa interrogante a los creyentes y planteó la necesidad de que cada persona pueda responderla desde su propia experiencia de fe. “¿Quién es Jesús para ti? Es lo más importante de mi vida. Eres la referencia que orienta mi vida”, expresó el cardenal durante su homilía. El líder de la Iglesia Católica en Honduras advirtió sobre la falta de formación religiosa que, a su juicio, enfrentan muchos niños y jóvenes. “Uno de los problemas que encontramos hoy día es que mucha juventud no conoce al Señor Jesús. No se lo han enseñado”, manifestó. Rodríguez cuestionó el papel de las familias en la transmisión de la fe y preguntó a los padres quién está enseñando a sus hijos quién es Jesús. Señaló que algunos jóvenes pueden participar en celebraciones religiosas, pero sin comprender plenamente el significado de las lecturas bíblicas o de la presencia de Jesús en la Eucaristía, debido a la falta de formación. Por ello, insistió en que el acercamiento a la fe debe comenzar desde los primeros años y contar con el acompañamiento de padres, familias, parroquias y espacios de catequesis. Uno de los principales llamados de Rodríguez estuvo dirigido a recuperar la oración dentro de los hogares. “¿Quién le enseña a rezar a los niños y a los jóvenes en el hogar?”, preguntó durante su reflexión, antes de advertir que actualmente “ya no se ora en familia”. Para el cardenal, la ausencia de estos espacios puede afectar la formación espiritual de las nuevas generaciones y dificultar posteriormente el desarrollo de una vida de fe. En ese contexto, pidió a las familias cristianas asumir la responsabilidad de transmitir a sus hijos el conocimiento de Jesús y mantener espacios de diálogo y reflexión. También llamó a no permitir que las nuevas tecnologías, incluida la inteligencia artificial, sustituyan los momentos de convivencia, reflexión y comunicación dentro de las familias. Durante su homilía, el cardenal también relacionó la pérdida de la fe con fenómenos que observa en la sociedad actual, entre ellos la soledad y el vacío interior. “La característica actual es cuánta soledad hay en una sociedad secularizada que prescinde de Dios. Soledad, vacío interior”, expresó. Ante esta situación, Rodríguez planteó la fe en Jesús como una fuente de esperanza y una referencia para la vida de los creyentes. El cardenal invitó a los fieles a redescubrir el Evangelio y fortalecer su relación con Cristo, más allá de una práctica religiosa limitada a asistir a misa. Rodríguez también reflexionó sobre las palabras de Jesús dirigidas a Pedro: “Tú eres Pedro y sobre esta piedra edificaré mi Iglesia”. Explicó que, desde la enseñanza del Evangelio, la Iglesia no se sostiene en ideologías ni intereses políticos, sino en la fe y la confianza en Jesucristo. Por ello, llamó a los católicos, especialmente a las nuevas generaciones, a renovar su relación con Cristo y a encontrar en la fe una referencia para sus decisiones y su vida cotidiana. Al concluir su homilía, el cardenal invitó a los fieles a hacer propia la respuesta de Pedro: “Tú eres el Mesías, el hijo de Dios vivo”, y a reconocer en Jesús un camino de libertad y esperanza.

data.title: Elche vs Barcelona, EN VIVO hoy: Su debut en la Liga Española
data.description: El Barcelona de Hansi Flick , campeón de las dos últimas ediciones de LaLiga EA Sports, inicia este domingo la defensa del título con una plantilla reforzada, a la que le falta concretar el fichaje de un delantero centro, ante un Elche que se agarra al apoyo del Estadio Martínez Valero. PARTIDO // Elche vs Barcelona EL 11 TITULAR DEL BARCELONA: Joan García; Eric García, Christensen, Gerard Martín, Espart; Gavi, Bernal, Fermín; Lamine Yamal, Adeyemi y Raphinha. EL 11 TITULAR DEL ELCHE: Dituro; Buba, Affengruber, Redondo, Chust, Valera; Villar, Aguado, Ali Houary; Morente y Niño. -- LA PREVIA -- El '9' es el único refuerzo que, de momento, no ha cerrado el director deportivo del club azulgrana, Anderson de Souza 'Deco', que sí ha conseguido incorporar futbolistas de nivel como los delanteros Anthony Gordon y Karim Adeyemi , el lateral Joao Cancelo y el centrocampista Rodrigo Hernández 'Rodri ', fichaje estrella de la temporada. Sin embargo, el capitán de la selección española, todavía sin ritmo de competición tras incorporarse esta semana a los entrenamientos, no debutará en Elche. Tampoco lo hará el extremo belga con ficha del filial Jesse Bisiwu, cuya inscripción todavía no ha sido validada por cuestiones burocráticas. Sin el ansiado delantero centro en la plantilla, Flick deberá decidir si apuesta por el joven '9' egipcio Hamza Abdelkarim, autor de cuatro goles en la pretemporada, o si ubica a uno de sus muchos extremos en la punta de ataque. En una pretemporada atípica por la disputa del Mundial de México, Estados Unidos y Canadá, el Barça llega con poco rodaje tras disputar tres partidos amistosos con un balance de dos victorias -ante el Al-Ahly (2-1) y el Basilea (2-5)- y un empate contra el Birmingham City (2-2). El Elche , por su parte, se estrena este domingo con la confianza que le dio el empate en Riazor (1-1) en su debut liguero. El conjunto ilicitano se agarra a un Martínez Valero que registrará un nuevo lleno y que fue clave la pasada temporada para lograr la permanencia, ya que el Elche solo cedió dos derrotas como local. La última fue precisamente ante el Barcelona (1-3), en enero, por lo que el equipo del técnico argentino Martín Anselmi buscará cambiar la historia y recuperar la fortaleza que mostró ante su público frente a un rival renovado, repleto de campeones del mundo, que ha vencido en sus últimas cinco visitas a Elche. Estadio: Martínez Valero. Hora: 1:30 pm (Honduras) Transmite: Sky Sports / ViX

data.title: Amhon pide “extremo cuidado” para 75 municipios en alerta roja por la sequía
data.description: Tegucigalpa, Honduras. Juan Carlos Molina, presidente de la Asociación de Municipios de Honduras ( Amhon ), pidió reforzar la atención en los 75 municipios declarados en alerta roja por la sequía asociada al fenómeno de El Niño y señaló que estas localidades requieren un “extremo cuidado”. “El tema de la sequía, voy a expresarles, ya ustedes saben que han sido elevados a alerta roja los 75 municipios que se han venido en observación. Han pasado de alerta roja, significa que ya amerita pues un extremo cuidado y una extrema atención a estos municipios”, declaró Molina a Radio Cadena Voces. La sequía afecta a gran parte del territorio hondureño. Aunque en los últimos días se han registrado algunos chubascos, las precipitaciones no han sido suficientes para aliviar la situación en las zonas más afectadas . Los 75 municipios permanecerán durante 120 días bajo alerta roja, mientras que el pasado 18 de agosto también se declaró alerta amarilla para 71 municipios y alerta verde para otros 88. Molina aseguró que las transferencias correspondientes a los gobiernos municipales se encuentran al día y señaló que el pago correspondiente a julio ya fue depositado a las alcaldías. “Estamos en el mes de agosto y el mes de julio ya se le depositó a todos los alcaldes”, afirmó. Sin embargo, ante la emergencia por la sequía, el presidente de la Amhon solicitó que se adelanten las transferencias correspondientes a agosto y septiembre para los municipios que se encuentran en alerta roja. “Y por eso pedimos anticipado para que agosto y septiembre se les depositara al menos a los 75 municipios”, explicó. Según Molina, 63 de los 75 municipios ya habían recibido esos fondos de manera anticipada, mientras que otros 12 aún estaban pendientes debido a uno o dos informes requeridos para completar el proceso. “Hay uno o dos informes pendientes que estamos con el equipo nuestro ayudándoles para ver cómo ellos resuelven”, indicó. El presidente de la Amhon señaló que distintas instituciones también han comenzado acciones para atender a las comunidades afectadas. data.translatedTitle: Amhon pide “extremo cuidado” para 75 municipios en alerta roja por la sequía
data.translatedDescription: Tegucigalpa, Honduras. Juan Carlos Molina, presidente de la Asociación de Municipios de Honduras ( Amhon ), pidió reforzar la atención en los 75 municipios declarados en alerta roja por la sequía asociada al fenómeno de El Niño y señaló que estas localidades requieren un “extremo cuidado”. “El tema de la sequía, voy a expresarles, ya ustedes saben que han sido elevados a alerta roja los 75 municipios que se han venido en observación. Han pasado de alerta roja, significa que ya amerita pues un extremo cuidado y una extrema atención a estos municipios”, declaró Molina a Radio Cadena Voces. La sequía afecta a gran parte del territorio hondureño. Aunque en los últimos días se han registrado algunos chubascos, las precipitaciones no han sido suficientes para aliviar la situación en las zonas más afectadas . Los 75 municipios permanecerán durante 120 días bajo alerta roja, mientras que el pasado 18 de agosto también se declaró alerta amarilla para 71 municipios y alerta verde para otros 88. data.title: Identifican a joven asesinada frente a una plaza en Comayagua
data.description: San Jerónimo, Comayagua. Una joven identificada como Génesis Acosta Morales fue asesinada a disparos durante la noche frente a una plaza ubicada en el sector de San Antonio de la Cuesta, San Jerónimo, Comayagua. De acuerdo con los reportes preliminares, la víctima residía en ese mismo municipio. Fue atacada a disparos por una persona durante la noche. Según informes preliminares, a Acosta Morales le dispararon en varias ocasiones y posteriormente huyeron de la escena. Hasta el momento no se ha informado sobre personas detenidas en relación con el crimen. Reportes locales confirmaron que el ataque ocurrió frente a una plaza del sector. Personas que se encontraban en el lugar alertaron a autoridades. Sin embargo, cuando los equipos de emergencia llegaron, Génesis Acosta ya no presentaba signos vitales. Agentes de la Policía Nacional acordonaron la zona para preservar posibles evidencias, mientras personal del Ministerio Público realizó las diligencias correspondientes. Las autoridades informaron que mantienen abierta la investigación.

data.title: Irán dice que considerará como enemigo a países que se unan a la guerra económica de EEUU
data.description: Irán advirtió que considerará como "enemigo" a los países que se unan a la "guerra económica" de Estados Unidos contra la República Islámica, una advertencia que llega después de que Washington anunciase un "DÍA D económico" contra el país persa. "Les decimos a todos los países vecinos que no se sumen a la guerra económica contra Irán. Cualquiera que lo haga será considerado un país enemigo", dijo el secretario del Consejo Supremo de Seguridad Nacional de Irán, Mohsen Rezaei, en una entrevista con la televisión estatal a última hora de anoche. "En primer lugar, negociaremos con ellos y les pediremos que no lo hagan; si continúan, tomaremos medidas contra ese país", añadió. El ex comandante en jefe de la Guardia Revolucionaria amenazó en concreto con atacar rutas de exportación de petróleo más allá del estrecho de Ormuz de países que colaboren en la campaña de presión económica estadounidense. Rezaei amenazó ademas con atacar intereses económicos estadounidenses si Washington procede con nuevas medidas financieras contra el país persa, como anunció. "No hemos atacado ningún interés económico estadounidense. Hasta ahora, solo hemos atacado bases militares, pero si pretenden imponernos sanciones económicas, Estados Unidos posee petróleo y empresas económicas en la región, y las atacaremos", dijo el exmilitar. El presidente de Estados Unidos, Donald Trump, ha anunciado "la operación económica más devastadora jamás emprendida contra cualquier país” en lo que denominó “un DÍA D económico” contra Irán para poner fin a una guerra que se acerca a los seis meses y reabrir Ormuz. Washington no ha anunciado aún en que consisten las nuevas medidas económicas contra la República Islámica, pero el secretario del Tesoro, Scott Bessent, advirtió a los países que proporcionen “cualquier tipo de ayuda vital a Irán” que sufrirán consecuencias económicas. Entre los principales socios comerciales de Irán se encuentran China, que adquiere en torno al 90 % del petróleo iraní a precio reducido, y Emiratos Árabes Unidos (EAU), que esta semana anunció la suspensión de todas sus relaciones comerciales, intercambios mercantiles y transacciones financieras con el país persa. La República Islámica lleva décadas sometida a sanciones económicas de Estados Unidos e internacionales, con por ejemplo la prohibición de vender su petróleo en los mercados internacionales, en unas medidas que han dañado gravemente la situación del país pero no han logrado doblegar a Teherán.

data.title: Teófimo López derrota a Rolly Romero y se corona campeón mundial wélter
data.description: El boxeador hondureño Teófimo López volvió a hacer historia en el boxeo al imponerse ante el estadounidense Rolly Romero y conquistar el título mundial wélter de la Asociación Mundial de Boxeo (AMB). El peleador de raíces hondureñas mostró su calidad, experiencia y determinación para quedarse con el cinturón y sumar un nuevo logro a su carrera profesional. Los jueces favorecieron a Teófimo con tarjetas de 116-112 y 115-113, mientras que una tercera marcó 114-114, permitiéndole conquistar el cinturón de las 147 libras. En una pelea de alto nivel y marcada por la intensidad de principio a fin, López mostró su experiencia, inteligencia y capacidad para imponerse ante Romero, consiguiendo una victoria que le permite sumar otro campeonato mundial a su exitosa carrera profesional. Con esta victoria, Teófimo López llega a 25 peleas como profesional, dejando su récord en 23 triunfos y dos derrotas. Sus únicos tropiezos en el boxeo profesional fueron ante George Kambosos Jr. y Shakur Stevenson, dos combates que marcaron momentos importantes en su carrera. Ahora, el boxeador de sangre hondureña vuelve a conquistar un cinturón mundial y se instala nuevamente entre los nombres destacados de las 147 libras. El título de la AMB abre la puerta a nuevos desafíos para Teófimo en una de las divisiones más competitivas y exigentes del boxeo internacional. Con el campeonato en sus manos, López podrá apuntar a grandes enfrentamientos ante otros protagonistas de la categoría y buscar nuevas noches de gloria. Su conquista en el peso wélter representa otro capítulo importante en una carrera en la que ya ha sido campeón mundial en tres divisiones diferentes. ¡Teófimo López vuelve a hacer historia! El boxeador de raíces hondureñas conquistó una nueva división al derrotar a Rolando “Rolly” Romero por decisión mayoritaria y convertirse en el nuevo campeón mundial del peso wélter de la WBA. GANÓ TEÓFIMO LÓPEZ Se termina la pelea y lo está celebrando Teófimo López a la falta del resultado. INICIA EL ÚLTIMO ASALTO: El undécimo. Fin del undécimo asalto: Teófimo López continúa manejando la distancia, entrando y saliendo con inteligencia y conectando golpes al cuerpo para controlar el ritmo del combate. Inicia el úndecimo round, ya es el penúltimo. Fin del décimo round: Teófimo López luce confiado, se mantiene activo y continúa controlando el ritmo del combate. En este asalto conectó un buen golpe a la cabeza de Rolly Romero que hizo retroceder al campeón, mientras López sigue entrando y saliendo con inteligencia para evitar las respuestas de su rival. Inicia el décimo round. Fin del noveno asalto : Rolly Romero necesita hacer algo diferente. El campeón ahora es quien persigue al retador, pero continúa lanzando pocos golpes y le cuesta encontrar a Teófimo López. El hondureño mantiene su estrategia, trabajando constantemente los planos bajos y conectando combinaciones que podrían estar sumándole importantes puntos en las tarjetas de los jueces. Inicia el noveno asalto. Fin del octavo round: Teófimo comienza a sentirse más cómodo sobre el cuadrilátero. El hondureño entra, conecta sus golpes y sale rápidamente de la zona de impacto, evitando quedar expuesto a las peligrosas contras de Rolly Romero. López está encontrando mejores espacios y manejando el ritmo del combate con mayor confianza. Inicia el octavo round. Fin del séptimo asalto:  Mientras Rolly Romero pelea a la contra, buscando conectar un golpe contundente que pueda cambiar el combate, Teófimo López apuesta por un boxeo de entrada y salida, combinando ataques a la cabeza y al cuerpo. Sin embargo, los golpes del hondureño no parecen llevar la misma potencia de otros asaltos, mientras Romero espera paciente su oportunidad para responder. Inicia el séptimo round. Fin del sexto round: ¡Teófimo se recupera y responde con autoridad! El hondureño se repuso tras el duro golpe del asalto anterior y terminó dominando el round. López trabajó muy bien los planos bajos, conectando combinaciones de dos y tres golpes que hicieron retroceder a Rolly Romero. Comienza el sexto asalto. Se acaba el quinto round y se lo llevó Rolly Romero. ¡Rolly Romero despierta y golpea con fuerza! El estadounidense conectó un tremendo zurdazo que provocó un corte en la ceja derecha de Teófimo López. El hondureño también sufrió una leve caída, en un momento de mucha tensión que cambia el rumbo del combate. Inicia el quinto round. ¡FIN DEL CUARTO ROUND!  Rolly Romero conectó un buen gancho de izquierda. Teófimo López continúa presionando y buscando imponer su ritmo sobre el cuadrilátero. Inicia el cuarto asalto. Termina el tercer round: Teófimo López continúa persiguiendo a Rolly Romero y buscando acortar la distancia, aunque sin descuidarse ante el peligroso gancho de izquierda del campeón. El estadounidense logró conectar una buena combinación de tres golpes que terminó inclinando la balanza a su favor en este asalto. Comienza el tercer asalto. ¡Se acaba el segundo round! Teófimo López está mezclando muy bien sus golpes, alternando ataques a la cabeza y al cuerpo de Rolly Romero. El hondureño lució más concentrado, preciso y paciente en este asalto, buscando imponer su ritmo y aprovechar cada oportunidad sobre el cuadrilátero. Inicia el segundo round. ¡Se acaba el primer round! Teófimo López tomó la iniciativa y salió decidido a buscar a Rolly Romero, presionando desde el inicio y tratando de imponer el ritmo de la pelea. El hondureño mostró una actitud agresiva. ¡Sonó la campana y comenzó la batalla! Teófimo López y Rolly Romero ya intercambian golpes sobre el cuadrilátero, en un esperado combate por el título mundial wélter de la AMB. El hondureño sale decidido a dejarlo todo y buscar la victoria en una noche que puede marcar su carrera. Teófimo López camino al cuadrilátero, su pasillo es con niños y jóvenes campeones en su categorías en lo amateur. Todo está listo para el gran combate. Teófimo López luce con orgullo la bandera de Honduras, llevando los colores de la patria al ring y representando a millones de catrachos que estarán pendientes de esta importante pelea.
